perspective:
From Harold Padilla’s perspective, the available information is:

- I am Harold, a project manager. Arthur Begum is a police officer and friend whom I rely on for advice.
- I felt frustrated and anxious that my project team seemed unmotivated, affecting progress. I arranged to meet Arthur at a coffee shop and told him I was at my wit’s end.
- Arthur told me motivation can be tricky and asked if I had tried understanding what drives each team member individually. He advised one-on-one conversations and making people feel valued and understood personally.
- I admitted I had focused on goals and deadlines, not personal motivations. I decided to try Arthur’s advice and felt hopeful.
- I told my team we would have quick one-on-one chats to understand their motivations. Team Member 1 said that could be helpful; Team Member 2 said they were open to it. I said I would schedule time with each of them and asked us to make the project a success together.
- Later, I noticed the team still was not responding well. I felt disappointed and worried about the project’s future, so I told Arthur I had tried his suggestions but the team still wasn’t responding.
- Arthur told me there might be deeper issues: personal conflicts, lack of trust, or external stressors. He suggested I dig deeper. I said I hadn’t thought of that and would set up another round of meetings.
- I became determined and focused, believing there might be underlying team issues. In one-on-one meetings, I asked team members to share concerns.
- Team Member 1 told me there was tension between a few team members affecting work. Team Member 2 told me they felt overwhelmed by the workload and stressed, which made motivation hard.
- I told them I would look into resolving conflicts and redistribute tasks to ease pressure, and that their well-being was important to me.
- I felt optimistic and empowered, believing that addressing individual concerns would improve performance. I announced regular feedback sessions and team-building activities to create a more supportive environment.
- Team Member 1 said that sounded great and would help; Team Member 2 agreed and said it was good concerns were being addressed. I said I was glad and emphasized that their input and well-being are crucial.

I do not have access to the private thoughts, hidden motives, or narrator-only information about Arthur or the team members beyond what they said or did in my presence.
